`docs/SPECFORGE_FEEDBACK_RESPONSE.md`, under `2026-09-26: Configuration, Verification And
Phase-Metadata Requests`, records required/optional scopes, dependencies and order for the supplied
packets. Parent `.33` owns them; intake `.33.1` implements none of those features.

2026-10-21 handoff acknowledges SPECFORGE `.7`–`.10`: durations and named
timers remain unimplemented; reset is answered at
`f6c44aa5a4517967632d25c2a190d2f1c2e22f59`. Record inputs were admitted at
`25c01f0127144922ade78951b91439e1d9221c08` and selected input qualification is
complete. Whole output/copy source admission is bounded; generated outputs,
member writes, runtime and full consumer delivery remain open. Root-list ports
and variants remain optional. Publication and caller integration are separate;
its register is read only. Request `.12` is owned by SEM `.92`. Book subsets
agree; old refused intakes stay historical. Status replies must reach the tracked
response as well as chat.

At `a7bf398ac3c1008b996bf0a92bdd18c9464d9fda`, native strict checks accepted `bogus-clause` and
unsupported `present` port options and emitted the same HDL as the clause-free control except its
date header. `_parse_interface` ignored malformed shapes and lacked final unknown-option rejection.
`.33.2` repairs this defect through the shared parser/native/API/MCP boundary: T1898 rejects
unsupported/malformed options in default and strict modes, preserving valid metadata.

Generic widths differ from earlier derived widths (`.32.3`): overriding HDL to 64 left default-32
WDATA at 32, while separately generating default-64 gave 64. Width dependencies were resolved before
emission. `.33.3` owns preservation; parameter legality and optional interfaces depend on it.

The positive-width undriven AWMECID and literal control lost their output role; a driven control
kept it. The FSM retained width but no role/drive marker, so unused-signal inference omitted it.
`.33.9` now carries both directions through `+interface`; T1900 qualifies native/API/MCP inventories
and HDL declarations. `.35` repairs the separate reset-only metadata-without-assignment gap, with
T1901 runtime proof.

The storage-register-access packet is retained in
`docs/audits/specforge-storage-register-access-intake-20260926.json`. Intake `.37` confirms
word-access refusal; `.38.1` owns independent scalar metadata and `.38.2` optional banks. Immediate
`.39.2.1` repairs ordinary/domain storage using the `.39.1` internal-role carrier. T1903 checks the
retained controls, direct FSM replay, exact interfaces, complete native/API/MCP parity, typed/unused
storage, bank elements and independent reset/write/read/hold behavior. The audit keeps the original
input/reset defect for falsification. T1904 qualifies ordinary/single-domain scalar/bank live reads,
exact interfaces and repeat activation. T1911 qualifies aggregate shapes; T1916 qualifies
independent-domain live reads and reset isolation. T1917/T1918 qualify sole scalar child writes
including independent domains; T1919 qualifies whole-record/list writers.
Partial/bank and competing writer qualification remains owned by .39.2.2.4.
Resolved reset widths reject overflow without
warnings. Explicit bindings and local state remain separate; decision `0107` owns shared semantics.

Audits retain exact caller bytes/hashes, native reports, output-role controls and the independent
HDL width oracle. Replay uses retained inputs and a fresh repository-relative same-volume
destination, capturing current outcomes without signing off changed behavior. Use a new destination
each time. Caller-wide impact counts were not independently measured; controls qualify neither the
whole caller corpus, future features nor four-state knownness.

id: specforge-handoff-query-timeout
title: SPECFORGE handoff gate query timeout remains causally open
answers:
  - "why did the SPECFORGE handoff gate fail?"
date: 2026-10-21
status: current
tags: [specforge, knowledge-map, verification]
evidence: docs/tasks/SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.md; docs/audits/specforge-request-status-20261021/second-gate-refusal.json.gz; docs/audits/specforge-request-status-20261021/query-diagnostic.json
reverify: scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- python3 -B docs/audits/specforge-request-status-20261021/query_verify.py
---

SEM `.91` retains the complete failed staged gate at native `15a9dceec`.
Its book byte-debt refusal is separate from the public Knowledge Map query
reaching `rollover_source_card.py`'s existing timeout. The overview is
consolidated within its unchanged allowance; feature details and examples stay.

SEM `.93` owns the query incident. The wrapper first discovers Git root, then
runs the Perl query over generated shards. Distinct bounded Git-root, wrapper
and direct-query diagnostics now succeed and return the expected route; their
new owned sessions settle. Their timings are informational and their process
placement differs from the original adapter. A passing control does not
attribute or repair the historical failure. Its execution-stage evidence is
missing; historical causality remains open. The normal gate must retain its
existing deadline and memory limits, with observation at the next required
qualification before publication. No host setting, source query, safety limit
or SPECFORGE feature was changed by these controls.

The first ad hoc passive observer failed decoding unrelated OS process arguments
as UTF-8. Its source and incomplete trace are retained as data; its executable
is retired. The component printed a positive footer, but that observer did not
retain a component exit status, so it does not qualify success. Its session was
absent at follow-up, with no signal needed. This is separate from the original
query timeout. The unchanged standard guard/component subsequently exits zero and confirms all
current public question routes. That qualifies the current check; historical
causality remains open.
